I farm 7.5 mu, so I cannot spread money around carelessly. I will start from what worked for me last year and only adjust a little. In Quzhou, the main income on my land still comes from the wheat-maize rotation, and with well irrigation I can push yield more steadily than dryland. So I will keep most of the land in wheat-maize, about 5 mu, and leave 2.5 mu for cotton. I do this because wheat and maize give me the safer grain output, while cotton can still bring cash if the price is decent. I have middle school education, so I do look at fertilizer balance, not only habit, but I still trust what I have seen in nearby fields. If neighbors who plant the same varieties get good stands and full ears or full bolls, I follow close to that. I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than let the crop go hungry, because losing yield hurts more than spending a bit more on inputs. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most fertilizer at base plus one topdressing at jointing, and irrigate around sowing, overwintering, and jointing or grain filling depending on moisture. For summer maize after wheat, I will usually go with hybrid seed, keep the straw handled quickly, use no-tillage or a very light pass so I do not lose time, and feed it enough nitrogen for a strong ear. For cotton, I will not plant too much because labor is tighter in my house with only 2 people, and cotton needs more watching for insects and more picking work. I will keep cotton on the better-managed piece, use improved seed, give it enough potash so the bolls set better, irrigate when it really needs it, and spray more times than wheat or maize because that is where I usually cannot save money.
